record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given an undirected graph G and another graph H as the parameter, is H topologically contained in G, meaning that some subdivision of H appears as a subgraph of G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph H is said to be topologically contained in a graph G if some subdivision of H (a graph obtained from H by replacing each edge with an internally disjoint path of length at least one) appears as a subgraph of G. Consider the following parameterized decision problem:

  Input: An undirected graph G.
  Parameter: An undirected graph H.
  Question: Is H topologically contained in G?

Determine whether this problem is fixed-parameter tractable; that is, decide whether there exists an algorithm that solves it in time f(|H|)·|V(G)|^{O(1)} for some computable function f.
artifact.status_search_result: Grohe, Kawarabayashi, Marx, and Wollan (STOC 2011, arXiv:1011.1827) proved that for every fixed graph H, one can test in O(|V(G)|^3) time whether G contains a subdivision of H, establishing fixed-parameter tractability of Topological Containment and resolving the open question of Downey and Fellows.

status_evidence.title: Finding topological subgraphs is fixed-parameter tractable
status_evidence.snippet: For every fixed undirected graph H, there is a O(|V(G)|^3) time algorithm that tests if H is contained in G as a topological subgraph.
status_evidence.claim: Topological Containment is FPT, with a cubic-time algorithm for every fixed H.

status_evidence.title: Reducing Topological Minor Containment to the Unique Linkage Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Grohe, Kawarabayashi, Marx, and Wollan resolved the parameterized complexity of the Topological Minor Containment problem by designing an algorithm with running time f(k)n^3.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms FPT resolution of Topological Containment.
